problem: The plotted curve is x = 0.05 sin(20t), which starts at x = 0 at t = 0. The worked example says the mass is pulled down 0.05 m and released from rest, so at t = 0 the displacement must be at its extreme value (+A if down is positive). Section 2 of the chapter itself states this rule (x = A cos ω_n t for release from rest), so the figure contradicts both the example and the text. A student matching the graph to the example will be confused about the phase.
fix: Plot x = 0.05 cos(20t) so the curve starts at +0.05 m at t = 0 and complete one cycle at 0.314 s; or keep the sine curve but relabel the figure as a generic SHM that starts at equilibrium (x = 0 at t = 0), not as the worked example.

problem: "1 Hz = 1 cycle/s = 2π rad/s" mixes two different quantities. Hz measures cycles per second; rad/s measures angular frequency. The correct link is ω = 2πf, so f = 1 Hz corresponds to ω = 2π rad/s. As written it reads like a unit conversion and sits awkwardly next to the advice to keep ω_n and f separate.
fix: "f is in Hz (cycles per second) and ω_n is in rad/s. They are linked by ω_n = 2πf, so f = 1 Hz corresponds to ω_n = 2π rad/s. Never quote ω_n as a frequency in Hz."

problem: "8 N/cm is 800 N/m, so the frequency changes by a factor of 10 in ω_n" is loosely worded: it does not say which way, and 'the frequency changes' sounds as if k itself changed. The point is what happens to the student's answer when the conversion is skipped.
fix: "8 N/cm is 800 N/m. If you substitute k = 8, you are out by a factor of 100 in k, so ω_n (and f) comes out 10 times too small."
